<meta>.purpose: Pins held back on purpose. A gitlink more than `--max-behind` commits behind its member's default branch is reported by the guard as drift; an entry here explains one instead. A held pin is a debt with an owner, not a steady state.
<meta>.required: Every entry needs `member` (the name under repos/), `reason` (why advancing the pin is currently wrong -- name the regression and the filed fix), and `reopen` (the observable event that retires the waiver). An entry missing any of them fails the check, so a waiver cannot decay into an unexplained hold.
<meta>.scope: Waivers cover drift only. A pin AHEAD of the member default -- a commit the member does not publish -- is reported as OFF-DEFAULT and is never waivable: it is not a pin held back, it is a pin pointing off the branch.

example.reason: ATLAS-EXAMPLE-2026-09-21: the default tip raises `oversized_files` 4 -> 6, which the conformance ratchet rejects
example.reopen: example PR #12 merges and the count returns to 4

<meta>.review: Re-verify every entry against the member's current default before a sweep advances pins; an entry whose regression the member has since fixed is deleted, not renewed. Measure it the way these were measured: `git -C repos/<member> archive FETCH_HEAD` into a scratch directory, then `python scripts/atlas-conformance.py check --repo <member> --member-path <dir>`, which judges the default tip against the committed baseline without touching the member checkout.
